title: The RateLimits contract splits setting a limit from consuming it: admin sets, controller may only spend
content:
A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.2.2.1.3.2 gates `setRateLimitData` on `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE`. A...1.3.4 and A...1.3.5 gate `triggerRateLimitDecrease` and `triggerRateLimitIncrease` on `CONTROLLER`.

The separation is what makes the limit a limit. If the controller could write `maxAmount`, every constraint it enforces on itself would be advisory — a compromised or buggy controller would simply raise the ceiling before spending. Instead the controller's only writes are movements of `lastAmount` **within** a ceiling it cannot touch, and `triggerRateLimitIncrease` is explicitly clamped: `newLimit = _min(currentRateLimit + amountToIncrease, maxAmount)`.

Stacked with the controller's own roles this yields four distinct authority levels: `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE` sets the envelope, `CONTROLLER` (the controller contract itself) consumes and restores within it, `RELAYER` triggers controller functions, and `FREEZER` can revoke the relayer. No single one of them can both widen a constraint and act under it.

The residual concentration is that `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE` on the RateLimits contract is the real seat of power in the whole Liquidity Layer — it can set any key to unlimited in one call — which is why it belongs to Sky governance rather than to Grove's operators.
description: setRateLimitData is onlyRole(DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE) while triggerRateLimitDecrease and triggerRateLimitIncrease are onlyRole(CONTROLLER), so a compromised controller can never raise its own ceiling.
